Multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis

Internal QC + R21 progress report

Bhattacharya Lab (analysis: S. Bresnahan; report generated with Biomni/Phylo)

2026-09-21

1 Executive summary

This report summarizes the multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis: cohort-only genotype PCA on LD-pruned variants within each ancestry stratum, a conventional covariate set (first 5 genotype PCs + HCP factors + sex, gestational age, and cell-type fractions, correlation-pruned and capped at ≤ 25), a MAF ≥ 0.01 filter with a ≥ 5 minor-allele-count floor at the genotype intersection, Storey q-values (computed with the R qvalue package), and log2(x + 1)-transformed isoform expression. Mapping covers 32 ancestry × modality × layer cells (EAS n ≈ 272, EUR n ≈ 136).

Headline result: two associations reach FDR ≤ 5%. An EAS isoform xQTL at TSPAN3 (q = 0.021; gene-level in the isoforms layer) and a EUR RNA-editing xQTL at an editing site in NCOA4 (ungrouped layer; q = 0.029; details below). Every other ancestry × modality × layer cell is null at FDR 5% — the best remaining q-value anywhere is 0.14. Storey calibration estimated at most a trace signal fraction (π1 = 0–4% across cells, concentrated in the layers carrying the hits), so the Storey q-values are numerically very close to Benjamini–Hochberg on this data (max |q − BH| = 0.006 on the combined layer; Diagnostics).

Three lines of evidence indicate the residual null is a power limitation, not a pipeline failure:

  1. Calibration is healthy — permutation-calibrated p-values track the null through the bulk in every layer (QQ plots, Diagnostics), and a near-zero π1 is the expected outcome when true effects are mostly below the detection floor.
  2. Detectable effect sizes remain large at our n — minimum detectable effect (80% power) is r² ≈ 0.10 at n ≈ 272 (EAS) and r² ≈ 0.19 at n ≈ 136 (EUR), versus ≈ 0.06 at PANTRY/Geuvadis n = 445. Typical cis-xQTLs explain 5–15% of phenotype variance — mostly below our floor. The two hits we do detect have estimated r² ≈ 0.13 (TSPAN3) and 0.3 (NCOA4) — exactly the class of outsize effect the floor permits.
  3. Sub-threshold tails are not shared between ancestries — cross-ancestry rank concordance of gene-level signal is ≈ 0, as expected if near-misses are noise rather than shared weak signal.

A carrier-count caveat applies to the EUR near-miss tail. The MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied at the genotype intersection before outlier exclusion; after removing PCA outliers (2 EAS, 5 EUR samples) and modality-specific sample attrition, a fraction of tested EUR variant–phenotype pairs retain 3–4 minor-allele carriers (audit table below). The EAS layers are clean (minimum 6 carriers anywhere). No FDR-significant result is carrier-limited, and all near-miss tables below flag carrier counts.

2 Data and methods

2.1 Pipeline recap

  • Phenotypes: 8 RNA modalities (gene expression, isoform expression, splice junction usage, intron retention, alternative TSS, alternative polyA, RNA editing, RNA stability), ComBat + quantile-normalized + inverse-normal transformed per ancestry, harmonized to genotyped samples (array_id), with NIGMS technical replicates averaged per individual. Isoforms are isoform expression values, log2(x + 1) transformed before ComBat.
  • Genotypes: ancestry-stratified plink2 pgen; variants filtered to MAF ≥ 0.01 with MAC ≥ 5 (≥ 5 minor alleles) at the genotype intersection — the count floor excludes low-carrier tests, which can produce spurious associations, while MAF 0.01 keeps the variant pool as large as defensible. tensorQTL’s own MAF ≥ 0.01 filter applies on top at mapping time.
  • Genotype PCA: cohort-only PCA per ancestry on LD-pruned variants (plink2 --indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2, then --pca 20 exact) — the GTEx convention.
  • Covariates: per ancestry, the pool of first-5 genotype PCs + HCP factors 1–15 + sex + gestational age + cell-type fractions (Syncytiotrophoblast as reference) was correlation-pruned (iterative max-|r| > 0.9 removal, protecting sex/GA > PCs > cell types > HCPs) and capped at ≤ 25 by dropping highest-index HCPs. The maternal cell-fraction covariate was excluded by analysis decision, leaving 24 covariates per ancestry (details and QC below).
  • Mapping (tensorQTL, cis window ±1 Mb): (i) per-modality grouped — all phenotypes of a gene within a modality tested as one group (permutation-calibrated gene-level p-value; the row label is the driver phenotype); (ii) combined — all phenotypes of a gene across all modalities as one cross-modality group (PANTRY’s headline design); (iii) ungrouped — per-phenotype lead variants for transcript-level resolution; (iv) stepwise (cis.map_independent) for conditionally independent signals, entered at FDR ≤ 5%.
  • Multiple testing: Storey q-values on the permutation-calibrated p-value (pval_beta), computed with the R qvalue package (default lambda) — the GTEx convention, and statistically identical to tensorQTL’s own calculate_qvalues. (On this cluster the rpy2/conda-R route to qvalue hits an unresolvable libstdc++/GLIBCXX conflict, so q-values are computed through a file-based bridge to the singularity R container used elsewhere in the pipeline.)

For reference, PANTRY (n = 445) reported 6,798 eGenes and a 66% discovery gain from non-expression modalities; GTEx tissues at n ≈ 150 typically report hundreds to ~2,000 eGenes. Our yield (two FDR hits, one of them gene-level) sits at the pessimistic end of that range.

5.1.1 EAS isoform xQTL at TSPAN3

The stronger of the two associations is gene-level: TSPAN3 isoform ENST00000267970 in the EAS isoforms layer. The lead variant 15:77800023:G:A sits 716 kb from the isoform TSS (within the ±1 Mb cis window), is common in EAS (AF = 0.36, 202 minor-allele carriers — far above the count floor), and has a moderate effect (slope = -0.54 on the inverse-normalized isoform level; nominal p = 6.8^{-9}; estimated r² ≈ 0.13). The association survives gene-level grouping within its modality (isoforms grouped q = 0.021), though not cross-modality grouping (combined q ≈ 0.15), and it is EAS-specific — the EUR isoforms layer is null for this gene (q ≈ 0.91), as is EAS gene expression (q ≈ 0.99). TSPAN3 (tetraspanin 3) encodes a cell-surface tetraspanin-family organizer; tetraspanins are implicated in trophoblast fusion and invasion in other contexts, but placental evidence for this locus specifically is thin — we present it as a candidate requiring visual QC of isoform levels by genotype and replication.

5.1.2 EUR RNA-editing xQTL at NCOA4

The second association is in the ungrouped EUR RNA-editing layer: editing site chr10:46,006,565, which lies inside the NCOA4 gene body (chr10:46,004,867–46,030,670). The lead variant 10:45322442:G:A sits 684 kb from the site, has AF = 0.05 with 14 minor-allele carriers (comfortably above the count floor), and a large effect (slope = -1.78 on the inverse-normalized editing level; nominal p = 1.4^{-8}; estimated r² ≈ 0.3). NCOA4 encodes the cargo receptor for ferritinophagy (selective autophagy of ferritin) — central to cellular iron handling, a core placental function.

Two tempering facts: (i) the same gene’s gene-level tests do not pass — EUR RNA-editing grouped q = 0.17 and combined q = 0.97 — so this is a single-phenotype association that does not survive the gene-level grouping burden; (ii) it is EUR-specific — the EAS stratum tests nearby editing sites in the same gene with different, common lead variants and is null (q ≈ 0.95–1.0), and the EUR lead variant (AF = 0.05 in EUR) is not the EAS lead for any NCOA4 site. With 14 carriers it clears the artifact floor, but visual QC of editing levels by genotype and replication in a larger EUR placental cohort are the required next steps before any functional claim.

5.3 Carrier-count caveat: the MAC floor did not fully propagate

Minimum minor-allele carrier counts per layer (mapping sample sets).
ancestry layer min_carriers n_lt5 n_total
EAS combined 6 0 12333
EAS grouped 6 0 32052
EAS ungrouped 6 0 48051
EUR combined 3 2052 12999
EUR grouped 3 8722 49428
EUR ungrouped 3 20809 114076

The MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied to the genotype intersection before PCA outlier exclusion; removing 2 EAS / 5 EUR outlier samples (plus small modality-specific sample differences) reduced carrier counts for the lowest-count variants. In EAS every tested pair retains ≥ 6 carriers; in EUR a fraction of tests retain 3–4 carriers in the mapping sample set (audit table). Consequences are contained — no FDR-significant result is carrier-limited, and the flagged tests would be removed by a post-hoc filter — but hit lists should be filtered to ma_count ≥ 5 (or report carrier counts alongside), and re-applying the count floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.

5.4 Stepwise regression: no secondary independent signals

No conditionally independent secondary signals were called in any ancestry × modality layer. The single FDR-qualifying group (EAS isoforms, TSPAN3) entered the stepwise scan and yielded only its primary lead variant (no group with >1 independent signal); every other cell had no FDR ≤ 5% entrant, so its stepwise output is empty by design.

7 Transcript-level driver resolution

The combined layer labels each gene-group by its driver phenotype (the phenotype with the best nominal association in the group), and the ungrouped layer provides per-phenotype lead variants. With only two FDR-significant associations, this machinery is applied mostly to the top-ranked near-misses for prioritization.

7.1 Driver-modality composition of top-ranked genes

Splicing drives the largest share of top-ranked genes in both ancestries (40% of the EAS top 50; 20% of the EUR top 50) — the same qualitative ordering PANTRY reported at n = 445. With only two FDR-significant associations, this is a descriptive property of the sub-threshold tail, not a discovery pattern.

8 Biological interpretation

The primary inferential statement is a near-null discovery landscape at genome-wide FDR, with two exceptions. At n ≈ 272 (EAS) and n ≈ 136 (EUR), with MAF ≥ 0.01 (+ MAC ≥ 5) and genome-wide permutation calibration, two associations reach FDR ≤ 5%: the EAS isoform xQTL at TSPAN3 and the EUR RNA-editing xQTL at NCOA4 described above. The TSPAN3 signal is the stronger of the two — it survives gene-level grouping within the isoforms layer and rests on 202 carriers — while the NCOA4 signal is phenotype-level only. Both have estimated effects (r² ≈ 0.13 and 0.30 respectively) in the class our power floor permits, and both are ancestry-specific. We present both as candidates requiring visual QC and replication, not established discoveries.

Beyond that, the landscape offers two hypothesis-generating observations:

  1. Splicing dominates the top tail in both ancestries, echoing PANTRY’s central finding that splicing modalities carry the largest share of non-expression regulatory signal. Isoform/junction regulation remains the modality most likely to yield placental discoveries as sample size grows — and the study’s only gene-level FDR hit is indeed an isoform QTL.
  2. Top-ranked genes (tables above) are prioritization hints only; the EUR top tail is contaminated by 3–4-carrier variants (flagged), reinforcing that sub-threshold rankings at our n should not be over-read.

9 Limitations and next steps

  1. Power. n ≈ 272/136 with a ~12k-gene testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects. Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY’s n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
  2. Carrier-count propagation. The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so 3–4-carrier tests persist in the EUR mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.
  3. Ancestry asymmetry. EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every modality (1.3–5.6×, modality-dependent; ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are restricted to genes tested in both.
  4. No pooled cross-ancestry inference was performed. If combined discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope meta-analysis are the clean options.
  5. No secondary stepwise signals — the only FDR-qualifying group (EAS isoforms, TSPAN3) yielded its primary lead variant alone; no conditionally independent secondary signal was called in any layer.
  6. Replication path: the TSPAN3 isoform xQTL and the NCOA4 editing xQTL are the priorities for lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for both.

10 Reproducibility

  • Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined / stepwise), MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, Storey q-values on pval_beta via the R qvalue package (singularity-R bridge). Covariates: 24 per ancestry as described (first-5 PCs + HCPs + sex/GA/cell types, correlation-pruned, capped, maternal fraction excluded). Genotype PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
  • Pipeline scripts: this repository (05_qtl_mapping/, scripts 19–30 + compute_qvalues.R; genotype pooling in 01_genotype_imputation/).
  • Report code: report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd + xqtl_report_functions.R; figures in figures/, tables in tables/.
  • Gene symbols: Ensembl REST lookup (current release at render date); NCOA4 (ENSG00000266412), REV3L (ENSG00000009413), TSPAN3 (ENSG00000140391), RNF220 (ENSG00000187147), and NAT14 (ENSG00000090971) verified against Ensembl/GENCODE v45.
